title: Tenant OOM tremor, slab flutter remediation and key-index journal rescue
creator: Asha Patel
description: Several tenants in hosted and dedicated pools experienced repeated GPU OOM cascades over the last 48 hours. Root cause appears to be a combination of aggressive per-session tensor arena growth (seen as 'slab flutter' in telemetry) and intermittent corruption of the key-index journal used to reconcile ephemeral cache entries. When the journal cannot be reconciled during session eviction, allocator backpressure is delayed and multiple sessions inflate memory until GPU OOMs trigger. This ticket coordinates triage, a minimal runtime hotpatch, and a safe rollback/rollout plan for hosted, dedicated, and Private customers.
symptoms_observed: hosted: burst of 5-10 tenants with GPU OOMs in 3m window
dedicated: tail latency + OOM spikes during sustained prefix-heavy workloads
private: single-customer isolated instance reported elevated slab churn and failed journal loads
initial_diagnosis: telemetry shows rapid arena allocations driven by long-running chat sessions with unbounded KV prefix growth
journal replay sometimes stops due to mismatched record checksums after concurrent compaction
allocator metrics indicate delayed eviction decisions when journal replay is blocked, causing memory pressure to cascade to GPU OOMs
steps_taken: 1) Captured heap + journal snapshot from an affected dedicated node (snap-20250218-02)
2) Reproduced slab flutter locally using a synthetic prefix-growth workload (repro-suite/gpu/oom-flutter)

3) Implemented a conservative hotpatch that: aborts journal replay on checksum mismatch and falls back to safe eviction path; limits per-session tensor arena growth with a soft cap; emits a distinct telemetry event 'kv_journal_desync'
4) Deployed hotpatch (canary) to 10 hosted hosts and 2 dedicated nodes for 2 hours with increased telemetry sampling
5) Notified affected customers and onboarded Solutions to monitor behaviors
decision_log: Reject full journal rebuild during canary (too invasive) — opted for graceful abort + fallback eviction to avoid prolonged service disruption
Enable checksum-safe abort rather than auto-heal to maintain reproducibility for post-mortem
Conservative soft cap on tensor arenas to buy time for eviction and avoid cold-start regressions
test_plan: Run repro-suite/gpu/oom-flutter at scale with canary binary across mixed seq-len profiles
Fuzz journal compaction and replay with checksum flips to validate safe-abort path
Tiered load tests to ensure soft cap does not regress latency under normal customer workloads
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): 10 hosted hosts + 2 dedicated nodes for 4h with elevated telemetry and auto-rollback on >3 OOMs. Phase 2 (Gradual): 25% of capacity over 12h if canary stable. Phase 3 (Full): 100% over 24h with post-rollout smoke tests and customer verification. Private customers will receive a patch bundle and guided upgrade window.
rollback_plan: Hotpatch includes a safe rollback toggle in runtime flags. If OOM rate or latency regresses beyond threshold, toggle will be flipped to restore previous behavior. For private deployments, coordinate with customer's infra lead and provide binary rollback package.
observed_results: Canary run showed 60% reduction in cross-session OOM cascades in the 2h window
Journal desync events surfaced distinct customers where compaction timing overlapped heavy mutation windows
Latency uplift <5% for worst-case tail during canary; SRE agreed acceptable for emergency patch
open_followups: Implement deterministic journal checksum repair utility (post-mortem task)
Long-term: redesign journal compaction to use atomic swap + versioning to avoid replay conflicts
Add guardrails in SDK to limit unbounded prefix growth from customer prompts
